title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice? (1 mark)
   A. A test of running
   B. A song
   C. A race in the field
   D. Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display

2. A sentence should end with a (1 mark)
   A. full stop
   B. comma
   C. drawing
   D. capital letter

3. Where should letters sit in a lined book? (1 mark)
   A. Outside the margin
   B. Above the page
   C. Under the desk
   D. On the base line

4. Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step? (1 mark)
   A. Then, wait.
   B. Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   C. First, wait.
   D. Next, wait.

5. Why should instructions be clear? (1 mark)
   A. So the listener can do the right thing
   B. So they are longer
   C. So people are confused
   D. So nobody listens

6. What does a comma tell a reader? (1 mark)
   A. To stop completely
   B. To turn the page
   C. To shout
   D. To take a short pause

7. Which sentence ends correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot:
   B. The sun is hot.
   C. The sun is hot?
   D. The sun is hot,

8. How do you show a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Read it faster
   B. Stop reading
   C. Raise your voice at the end
   D. Whisper

9. Which sentence has a verb? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau washed his face.
   B. In the morning.
   C. Kamau and his face.
   D. The red bag.

10. Which word shows the first step? (1 mark)
   A. Finally
   B. First
   C. In the end
   D. Lastly

11. Why should you not translate a saying from your language word for word? (1 mark)
   A. The meaning may be lost
   B. Words are never important
   C. It is always easy
   D. It is against the law

12. What does the Kiswahili proverb Haba na haba hujaza kibaba teach? (1 mark)
   A. Only large amounts count
   B. Big things are useless
   C. Never save
   D. Small amounts added together become a lot

13. How should a proverb be used in a composition? (1 mark)
   A. With no meaning
   B. In a way that fits the story
   C. Only at the start
   D. Anywhere at all

14. Which sentence joins two events with when? (1 mark)
   A. I smiled the gift.
   B. Saw I gift.
   C. I smiled when I saw the gift.
   D. When the gift.

15. What is the language train game? (1 mark)
   A. A reading test
   B. Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   C. A running race
   D. A game with real trains

16. Which question helps you plan an experience to tell? (1 mark)
   A. Who was there?
   B. How long is the ruler?
   C. Where is the moon?
   D. What colour is the wall?

17. Where should the comma go in I have money and I want a book? (1 mark)
   A. After want
   B. Before and
   C. After I
   D. After have

18. The ball is touching the top of the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. behind
   C. on
   D. outside

19. Which is an example of caring for an animal? (1 mark)
   A. Giving clean water every day
   B. Beating it
   C. Leaving it without shelter
   D. Throwing stones at it

20. What does rhyme mean? (1 mark)
   A. Words with the same ending sound
   B. Words with many letters
   C. Words with no vowels
   D. Words with capital letters

21. What does pace mean when reading a poem? (1 mark)
   A. How long the poem is
   B. How many words rhyme
   C. How loud you read
   D. How fast or slow you read

22. What is spoken word? (1 mark)
   A. A silent song
   B. A dictionary
   C. Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   D. A kind of drawing

23. How should peer feedback be given? (1 mark)
   A. Rudely
   B. Never
   C. Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   D. Loudly

24. What is the problem in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The trouble or challenge the characters face
   B. The ending word
   C. The page
   D. The title

25. What are the events of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The margin
   B. What happens step by step
   C. The title
   D. The author

26. What is a digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A wooden tool
   B. A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   C. A kind of fruit
   D. A type of song

27. What is a call centre? (1 mark)
   A. A farm
   B. A market
   C. A school
   D. A place where staff answer customers' phone calls

28. Which adjective describes shape? (1 mark)
   A. loud
   B. red
   C. heavy
   D. round

29. What should a newsreader do? (1 mark)
   A. Speak clearly at a steady pace
   B. Shout
   C. Skip words
   D. Mumble

30. What is news? (1 mark)
   A. Information about recent events
   B. Old stories only
   C. Songs
   D. Riddles

31. Which of these is an adjective in Fresh sweet oranges? (1 mark)
   A. sweet
   B. for
   C. sale
   D. oranges

32. What does a signature show? (1 mark)
   A. Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   B. The paper size
   C. The colour of a pen
   D. The price of a form

33. Which word in The teacher counted the votes is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. votes
   B. the
   C. teacher
   D. counted

34. What does a moderator do in a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeps
   B. Leaves
   C. Guides the discussion and gives turns
   D. Speaks all the time

35. What should a real-life experience description include? (1 mark)
   A. Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   B. Nothing
   C. Only a number
   D. Only a title

36. What is a stanza? (1 mark)
   A. A group of lines in a poem
   B. A rhyme only
   C. The title
   D. A single word

37. What is a poem's title? (1 mark)
   A. Its name
   B. Its last line
   C. Its rhyme
   D. Its page

38. What should you use in your answers to poem questions? (1 mark)
   A. Words from the poem
   B. Your favourite song
   C. A dictionary only
   D. Nothing

39. Which is a verb in Open your book? (1 mark)
   A. Open
   B. the
   C. book
   D. your

40. What is the treasure hunt game used for? (1 mark)
   A. Learning to sing
   B. Practising following instructions
   C. Drawing maps only
   D. Sleeping

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)

42. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

43. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)

44. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

45. Write four numbered steps for crossing a road safely. (4 marks)

46. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

47. Explain what intonation is and give one English example of a rising voice. (2 marks)

48. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

49. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

50. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

51. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)

52. What is a paragraph and what is its main idea? (2 marks)

53. Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community. (4 marks)

54. Name two components of a poem. (2 marks)

55. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

56. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)

57. Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains. (3 marks)

58. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

59. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

2. A — full stop
   A statement ends with a full stop.

3. D — On the base line
   Letters rest on the base line.

4. B — Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   Finally shows the last step.

5. A — So the listener can do the right thing
   Clear instructions prevent mistakes.

6. D — To take a short pause
   Commas show short pauses.

7. B — The sun is hot.
   A statement ends with a full stop.

8. C — Raise your voice at the end
   Questions often rise at the end.

9. A — Kamau washed his face.
   Washed is the verb.

10. B — First
   First begins the sequence.

11. A — The meaning may be lost
   Sayings often carry meaning beyond the words.

12. D — Small amounts added together become a lot
   The proverb means little by little fills the measure.

13. B — In a way that fits the story
   A proverb should match the lesson of the story.

14. C — I smiled when I saw the gift.
   It uses when to link two events.

15. B — Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   Each pupil adds a when sentence.

16. A — Who was there?
   Who, what, where, when, why and how help plan a story.

17. B — Before and
   A comma comes before the joining word.

18. C — on
   On shows contact with the top.

19. A — Giving clean water every day
   Water and shelter meet its needs.

20. A — Words with the same ending sound
   Rhyming words sound alike at the end.

21. D — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is speed.

22. C — Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   Spoken word is performed poetry.

23. C — Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   Kind feedback helps writers.

24. A — The trouble or challenge the characters face
   The problem drives the events.

25. B — What happens step by step
   Events are the actions in order.

26. B — A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   Phones and computers are digital devices.

27. D — A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   Call centre staff answer calls.

28. D — round
   Round describes shape.

29. A — Speak clearly at a steady pace
   Clear speech helps listeners.

30. A — Information about recent events
   News reports what has happened.

31. A — sweet
   Sweet describes the oranges.

32. A — Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   A signature confirms you agree.

33. D — counted
   Counted shows the action.

34. C — Guides the discussion and gives turns
   The moderator keeps order.

35. A — Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   These details make it clear.

36. A — A group of lines in a poem
   A stanza is a group of lines.

37. A — Its name
   The title names the poem.

38. A — Words from the poem
   Answers should come from the poem.

39. A — Open
   Open is the action.

40. B — Practising following instructions
   Each note gives the next instruction.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1. Stop at the edge. 2. Look right, left and right. 3. Listen for vehicles. 4. Cross when the road is clear.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in a sensible order.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice as we speak. A question such as Are you coming? rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for a correct example.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one topic. The main idea is what it is mostly about.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct steps.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, message (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
   Working / marking points: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.
